roots.name: Roots
roots.blurb: From Edo caricature to Tezuka. Where all of it begins.

shonen.name: Shonen
shonen.blurb: What the weekly boys' magazines built: effort, friendship, victory — and the dark fantasy that came after.

shojo.name: Shojo & Josei
shojo.blurb: The expressive revolution of the Year 24 Group: interiority, romance, BL, josei.

seinen.name: Seinen
seinen.blurb: Manga for adults, born out of gekiga. Realism, society, work, science fiction.

gag.name: Gag & Comedy
gag.blurb: The lineage of laughter Akatsuka Fujio systematised — nonsense, absurdism, and the slice-of-life that followed.

alt.name: Alternative
alt.blurb: The experimental spirit of Garo and COM, expanding what manga could do from outside the commercial mainstream.

digital.name: Digital & New Currents
digital.blurb: The shapes manga takes once the web, the smartphone and social media arrive.

notes.berubara: The palace of Versailles on the eve of revolution, and the cobbled streets Oscar rode through

notes.thermae: The imperial capital in the 2nd century, and the public baths Lucius designed

notes.kaze_ki: Late 19th century — the dormitory of Lacombrade Academy is where the story lives

notes.poe: A clan of vampanella travelling through time, setting out from 18th-century Britain

notes.shingeki: A real town ringed by a circular wall, often named as the model for the world inside the walls

notes.golgo: A sniper of the first rank whose workplace is the whole world; the skyscraper shot is a staple

notes.sololeveling: Seoul, where gates and dungeons have opened — and also the home city of webtoons

notes.akira: Neo Tokyo, 2019. A future city built on top of the old one
notes.tetsuwan: Tokyo in the 21st century, where robots and people live together — a future we have now passed

notes.kingdom: China at the end of the Warring States period, as Xin and Ying Zheng set out to unify it

notes.vinland: The 11th century, the Viking age. Thorfinn's revenge, and his recovery

notes.monster: The city of the Eisler Memorial Hospital where Tenma worked; the story spreads across Germany

notes.historie: The life of Eumenes, the scribe who served Alexander the Great

notes.onepiece: An ocean that appears on no map. The voyage around the world starts here

notes.tensura: Reborn off the edge of the map — the Jura Forest of sword and sorcery

notes.chojugiga: The temple that holds the Choju-jinbutsu-giga scrolls: where you can meet Japan's oldest manga

notes.goldenkamuy: Hokkaido in the late Meiji years. Gold, Ainu culture, hunting and food

notes.ginsaji: Ooezo Agricultural High School. Vast fields, livestock, and lessons in eating

notes.kimetsu: Tanjiro's home is Mt. Kumotori; the story opens in Taisho-era Tokyo Prefecture

notes.tondesaitama: Saitama residents strike back against their Tokyo oppressors — affectionate hometown comedy
notes.crayon: The Nohara family of Kasukabe. Shin-chan is the city's official parenting-support character

notes.initiald: The pass down Akina that the Hachi-Roku takes; modelled on the winding roads of Mt. Haruna

notes.bluegiant: The city where Dai kept playing tenor sax on the banks of the Hirose River

notes.chihaya: The sacred ground of competitive karuta, home of the Master and Queen title matches

notes.deathnote: Police HQ and L's task force — the stage for Light Yagami's war of wits
notes.sailor: Set in Azabu-Juban; a real shopping street with a trace of Sailor Moon about it
notes.oishinbo: The Tozai Shimbun. Many of the restaurants are modelled on real ones in Tsukiji and Ginza
notes.shima: Hatsushiba Electric's head office. Salaryman Tokyo of the Showa years
notes.conan: Beika Town. Probably the highest crime rate in Japan
notes.azumanga: The everyday life of a Tokyo high school that could be anywhere

notes.ashita: The doss houses of San'ya and Namida Bridge — where Joe got back on his feet
notes.kyojin: Training with the major-league ball harness in a row house, with his father Ittetsu
notes.wani: A hundred ordinary days in a Tokyo that could be anywhere

notes.urusei: Tomobiki Town is modelled on the suburbs west of Tokyo; Mizuki's Chofu is close by

notes.slam: The Shohoku basketball team. The Enoshima line crossing became a landmark for fans worldwide

notes.chibimaruko: Shimizu in 1974, and the walk to school with Maruko and Tama-chan

notes.chie: The offal restaurant Chie runs. A working-class city with Kansai warmth

notes.gegege: Shigeru Mizuki's hometown; Mizuki Shigeru Road holds 177 bronze yokai

notes.cookingpapa: The Araiwa family dinner table — Hakata, and over 1,500 recipes you can actually cook

notes.barakamon: The island the calligrapher Handa moved to. Dialect, the sea, and children

emaki.desc: The caricature tradition typified by the Choju-jinbutsu-giga scrolls, where movement and comedy are carried by brushed ink lines alone. There are no panels and no speech balloons, so the direct bloodline to modern manga is thin — but as the oldest high point of telling a story through pictures, it is often called manga's ancestor.

edo_giga.desc: The caricature ordinary people of Edo grew up with: Hokusai Manga, Toba-e, kusazoshi picture books. The word manga here meant a sketch drawn as the hand pleased, quite different from today's sense — but the word, and a public used to reading pictures, both carried into the modern era.

ponchi.desc: Starting with satirical drawings in magazines like Marumaru Chinbun, Rakuten Kitazawa established manga as a profession and a job title. Together with Ippei Okamoto's illustrated essays, this is where modern Japanese manga starts.

newspaper.desc: Shochan no Boken and Nonki na Tousan became enormously popular, and the format of a continuing story told in panels with speech balloons settled here. After the war, Sazae-san made the newspaper strip a national institution.

kodomo.desc: Norakuro and Boken Dankichi in Shonen Club were runaway hits, and a market for children's manga came into being. The shape of the collected-volume business starts here too.

kamishibai.desc: Street-corner picture-card theatre was a major entertainment for children before and after the war. Shigeru Mizuki, Sanpei Shirato and other future masters of gekiga and horror sharpened their storytelling craft here.

akahon.desc: Cheap, roughly made manga volumes born in postwar Osaka. Out of that mixed market came the debut of Osamu Tezuka, and manga history began to move.

story.desc: Tezuka's New Treasure Island hit young readers with cinematic panel-to-panel movement. Story manga — telling a long narrative in comics — became the parent of essentially every genre that follows.

kashihon.desc: Volumes drawn specifically for rental shops. This was the laboratory for gekiga, horror and shojo alike, and it produced Yoshiharu Tsuge, Kazuo Umezu and Takao Saito.

gekkan.desc: The era of Manga Shonen and Shonen. Astro Boy and Tetsujin 28-go ran here, and the young artists of Tokiwa-so — Fujiko Fujio, Shotaro Ishinomori, Fujio Akatsuka — grew up in it.

weekly.desc: In 1959 Shonen Magazine and Shonen Sunday launched on the same day. The weekly serialisation system became the skeleton of the manga industry; Shonen Jump followed in 1968.

yokai.desc: Shigeru Mizuki, who came up through kamishibai and rental manga, set off a yokai boom with GeGeGe no Kitaro. Together with Umezu's horror, it gave Japanese manga a lasting lineage of the other world.

spokon.desc: Star of the Giants and Tomorrow's Joe. The gekiga heat that writer Ikki Kajiwara brought in, and the drama of effort and sheer will, became the template for the shonen manga that followed.

lovecome.desc: Rumiko Takahashi's Urusei Yatsura and Mitsuru Adachi's Touch. They carried shojo manga's way of drawing romance into boys' magazines and built Shonen Sunday's golden decade in the 1980s.

jump_battle.desc: Dragon Ball, Fist of the North Star, Saint Seiya. Friendship, effort, victory — plus the tournament-arc formula — carried Jump to a peak circulation of 6.53 million copies.

shonen_mystery.desc: The lineage DEATH NOTE opened up, where the fight is replaced by wits. The particular tension of The Promised Neverland or Kaiji became a new staple of boys' magazines.

dark_fantasy.desc: After the shock of Attack on Titan, battle manga that faces death and despair head-on — Demon Slayer, Chainsaw Man — moved into the mainstream, and the border with seinen manga dissolved.

isekai.desc: The reborn-in-another-world boom came out of web-novel sites and exploded once it was drawn as manga. That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime and Re:Zero mark the moment web-born work became an industry.

shojo_dawn.desc: Tezuka's Princess Knight laid out the shape of story manga for girls. Ribon and Nakayoshi launched, and a market for shojo manga stood up.

kashihon_shojo.desc: Women artists such as Masako Watanabe and Hideko Mizuno came to the front. Across rental books and monthly magazines, shojo manga worked out its grammar — from tears-and-mothers to full-blooded romance.

year24.desc: Moto Hagio's The Poe Clan, Keiko Takemiya's Kaze to Ki no Uta, Yumiko Oshima. Artists born around 1949 brought interiority, science fiction and boys' love into shojo manga and pushed it to a literary height.

shojo_romance.desc: The Rose of Versailles, Aim for the Ace!, Glass Mask. Sweeping dramas of fate and passion set against history, sport and the stage became the flagship of girls' magazines.

bl.desc: The boys' love expression of the Year 24 Group led to the magazine JUNE, and commercial BL imprints were established in the 1990s. It is now a genre born in Japan with a worldwide market.

ladies.desc: Manga for adult women, born as shojo readers grew up. It drew love, marriage and work with a plain realism, and led on to the josei manga of later decades.

shojo_horror.desc: Out of the girls'-magazine horror tradition running from Umezu came the dedicated horror magazine Halloween, which produced artists with worldwide cult followings such as Junji Ito.

battle_bishojo.desc: Sailor Moon connected the structure of the battling hero to shojo manga. The fighting girl became a central image of Japanese pop culture from then on.

gekiga.desc: Yoshihiro Tatsumi and the Gekiga Kobo group declared themselves against Tezuka's round-lined children's manga. With realistic drawing and adult subjects, they raised the age of the manga reader.

seinen_mag.desc: Young Comic and Big Comic launched and became the home gekiga needed. Golgo 13 is still running, at a length that belongs in the record books.

gekiga_jidai.desc: Lone Wolf and Cub, and Hiroshi Hirata's samurai work. The fusion of period drama and gekiga was exported: Lone Wolf and Cub had an enormous influence on American comics artists.

seinen_sf.desc: Katsuhiro Otomo's AKIRA and Masamune Shirow's Ghost in the Shell. Dense drawing and a sense of the city ending are what made Japanese comics known abroad as MANGA.

gourmet.desc: Oishinbo invented a way to make food itself the drama. From Cooking Papa to The Solitary Gourmet, it grew into a large genre with no real equivalent elsewhere.

business.desc: Section Chief Kosaku Shima, Naniwa Kinyudo. Salaryman society, the back rooms of finance — this is where manga established itself as a way to learn how the world works.

gamble.desc: Nobuyuki Fukumoto's Akagi and Kaiji. Carrying on the gekiga drawing style, it built a genre of its own out of psychological warfare at the limit, held in that famous rustling tension.

shakai.desc: The Silent Service, Give My Regards to Black Jack, A Minimum Standard of Healthy and Cultured Living. The lineage where manga takes on the work of reporting and long-form journalism.

akatsuka.desc: Osomatsu-kun and Genius Bakabon. Fujio Akatsuka systematised character-driven gag manga; his catchphrase that this is fine, as it is, was gag manga's declaration of independence.

nonsense.desc: Gaki Deka and Makaroni Horenso. In the pages of 1970s Shonen Champion, gag accelerated into an age of high tension and release from meaning.

yonkoma.desc: Out of the newspaper four-panel tradition (Sazae-san, Kobo-chan) came dedicated four-panel magazines such as Manga Time. Its setup-and-punchline form became the soil for slice-of-life.

fujori.desc: Senshya Yoshida's Utsurun Desu took the four-panel structure apart. It made the word surreal stick in Japanese and came to stand for the subculture sensibility of the 1990s.

moe_yonkoma.desc: Azumanga Daioh invented the unremarkable everyday life of cute girls. Through K-On! and Yuru Camp, it made a case for the richness of nothing much happening.

garo.desc: The legendary magazine Garo, founded so that Sanpei Shirato's Kamui-den could run. With work like Tsuge's Neji-shiki, it became the sanctuary for experiment free of commercial pressure.

com.desc: COM, launched by Tezuka in answer to Garo. Billed as a manga magazine for manga elites, it serialised Phoenix and became a birthplace of manga criticism.

newwave.desc: The turning point marked by Otomo's arrival. A dry line and cinematic space that belonged to neither gekiga nor Tezuka rebuilt what manga could look like in the 1980s.

subculture.desc: AX, carrying Garo's genes, plus artists like Nekojiru and Suehiro Maruo. Within 1990s subculture they gathered a devoted cult following.

essay.desc: My Darling is a Foreigner opened up the genre of telling your own experience in loose, friendly drawing. Parenting, illness, work — manga became a container for non-fiction.

webcomic.desc: ONE's One Punch Man, which began on a personal website, is the emblem. A place to publish without a publisher became an entrance for talent, and official web magazines such as Ura Sunday followed.

webtoon.desc: Full-colour vertical-scroll comics, born in Korea and built for the phone. Through Piccoma and LINE Manga they grew fast in Japan too, and now compete and blend with panel-layout culture.

sns.desc: A Crocodile That Lives 100 Days, born on Twitter, became a social phenomenon. Short one-to-four-page pieces made for sharing, and an unusually short distance between artist and reader.

chojugiga.title: Choju-jinbutsu-giga (Frolicking Animals)
chojugiga.desc: Four scrolls drawn in ink line alone, in which rabbits and frogs wrestle and play in the water. The living line and the exaggerated animal acting have earned it the name of Japan's oldest manga. It is in fact the work of several hands, and has neither panels nor dialogue — but as a high point of making story and comedy out of pictures alone, it belongs here.

hokusai.title: Hokusai Manga
hokusai.desc: Around 4,000 sketches Hokusai published as a drawing manual for his students. Figures, plants and animals, yokai, and the offhand gestures of ordinary townspeople — and it is this book that spread the word manga. It has no story and no panels, so it is a different thing from manga today, but it stands for a culture in which ordinary people enjoyed pictures.

norakuro.title: Norakuro
norakuro.desc: The stray dog Kurokichi works his way up through the army. The biggest hit of the prewar years, and the first manga to be merchandised as a character.

shintakarajima.title: New Treasure Island
shintakarajima.desc: Cinematic, fast-moving panel work that hit postwar boys hard and opened the age of story manga. A landmark.

tetsuwan.title: Astro Boy
tetsuwan.desc: A monument of science fiction about robots and humans living together. In 1963 it became Japan's first weekly TV anime series, and the starting point of the media mix.

ribon_kishi.title: Princess Knight
ribon_kishi.desc: The adventures of Princess Sapphire, raised as a boy. It laid out the shape of story manga for girls, and its Takarazuka-like world flowed into the shojo manga that followed.

kamui.title: The Legend of Kamui
kamui.desc: A sweeping gekiga about the rigid class system of the Edo period. The magazine Garo was founded so this could run. A bible for the student-movement generation.

gegege.title: GeGeGe no Kitaro
gegege.desc: The cornerstone of yokai manga, developed out of the kamishibai serial Kitaro of the Graveyard. Much of what Japanese people picture when they hear yokai was made here.

kyojin.title: Star of the Giants
kyojin.desc: A baseball manga that bets everything on a father-and-son destiny and an impossible pitch. It defined the sports-and-guts genre itself.

ashita.title: Tomorrow's Joe
ashita.desc: A boxing gekiga following Joe Yabuki, a boy out of the doss houses, until he burns out. When Toru Rikiishi died, a real funeral was held for him.

neji.title: Neji-shiki (Screw Style)
neji.desc: A 23-page short story that proceeds by the logic of a dream. It is what made manga a subject for art criticism, and remains the summit of alternative manga.

golgo.title: Golgo 13
golgo.desc: The work of Duke Togo, a sniper of the first rank. It holds the world record for the most volumes of a single manga, and is the high point of gekiga.

devilman.title: Devilman
devilman.desc: Human malice drawn on an apocalyptic scale, pushing past what boys' manga was thought able to say. The ancestor of later dark fantasy.

poe.title: The Poe Clan
poe.desc: Edgar, a vampanella boy who lives forever. A cycle of stories about time and solitude, generally counted as shojo manga's literary summit.

berubara.title: The Rose of Versailles
berubara.desc: The life of Oscar, a woman living as a man, set against the French Revolution. It became a social phenomenon and one of the Takarazuka Revue's signature works.

blackjack.title: Black Jack
blackjack.desc: An unlicensed genius surgeon asking what a life is worth — the origin of medical manga, and the major work of Tezuka's later years.

kaze_ki.title: Kaze to Ki no Uta (The Poem of Wind and Trees)
kaze_ki.desc: A story of love between boys at a French boarding school in the 19th century. Nine years in the planning, and the source of what became BL.

garasu.title: Glass Mask
garasu.desc: The cornerstone of theatre manga, following the growth of the prodigy actress Maya Kitajima. A long-running series that produced one legend after another.

urusei.title: Urusei Yatsura
urusei.desc: A screwball romantic comedy between the alien Lum and the incorrigible Ataru. Takahashi's method of blending science fiction, gags and romance shaped everything after it.

touch.title: Touch
touch.desc: Twin brothers and the girl next door, Minami. It swapped the heat of sports-and-guts for monologue and empty space — the emblem of Shonen Sunday in the 1980s.

nausicaa.title: Nausicaa of the Valley of the Wind
nausicaa.desc: A thousand years after a vast industrial civilisation fell, in a far future menaced by the Sea of Decay and its insects. The seven volumes go well past the film, and make an epic full of questions about life and civilisation that good and evil cannot settle.

hokuto.title: Fist of the North Star
hokuto.desc: Kenshiro inherits an assassination art passed to one heir per generation, in a wasteland at the end of the world. Gekiga's bodies fused with Jump's battles.

oishinbo.title: Oishinbo
oishinbo.desc: Ultimate versus Supreme, menu against menu. It brought both connoisseurship and drama to food, and established gourmet manga as a genre.

shima.title: Section Chief Kosaku Shima
shima.desc: The byword for salaryman manga: climbing the ladder inside a major electronics maker. Its hero has since been president and chairman, and is still going.

dragonball.title: Dragon Ball
dragonball.desc: From a hunt for seven balls to the summit of the battle manga. One of the largest pop icons of the 20th century, felt across boys' manga, American comics and games alike.

tomie.title: Tomie
tomie.desc: Tomie, a beautiful girl who multiplies however often she is killed. Born in a girls' horror magazine, it is the representative horror manga with a cult following worldwide.

sailor.title: Sailor Moon
sailor.desc: In the name of the Moon, I'll punish you. It created the template for the transforming heroine team and rewrote girls' culture around the world.

kaiji.title: Kaiji: Ultimate Survivor
kaiji.desc: Restricted rock-paper-scissors; walking the steel beam. A young man in debt stakes his life on gambling — the byword for psychological warfare at the limit.

azumanga.title: Azumanga Daioh
azumanga.desc: The unremarkable everyday life of high-school girls, in four panels. The starting point of the slice-of-life genre.

darling.title: My Darling is a Foreigner
darling.desc: Daily life with her foreign husband Tony; over a million copies sold. The book that lit the comic-essay boom.

shingeki.title: Attack on Titan
shingeki.desc: A hopeless war between the humans inside the walls and the titans outside. A story of foreshadowing and structure that changed the landscape of 2010s manga.

onepunch.title: One Punch Man
onepunch.desc: The troubles of a hero who can beat any enemy in one punch. From a personal website to a social phenomenon — the emblem of web-born manga.

tensura.title: That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime
tensura.desc: An office worker stabbed by a stranger is reborn as a slime. The biggest hit among the web-novel adaptations.

kimetsu.title: Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba
kimetsu.desc: The story of Tanjiro, whose family was killed by demons. Taisho design, Japanese motifs and the uncanny, multiplied by the anime, produced a historic boom.

chainsaw.title: Chainsaw Man
chainsaw.desc: Denji, a boy fused with the chainsaw devil. Cinematic quotation and an amoral momentum keep pushing at what Jump is supposed to be.

sololeveling.title: Solo Leveling
sololeveling.desc: A Korean webtoon in which the weakest hunter levels up alone. A huge hit that stands for vertical-scroll full colour opening up the Japanese market.

wani.title: A Crocodile That Lives 100 Days
wani.desc: A hundred-day countdown to a death, posted one page a day. An experiment in which the publishing format itself — social media — became part of the story.

chie.title: Jarinko Chie
chie.desc: Chie, a grade-schooler running an offal restaurant in working-class Osaka. A Kansai-dialect comedy of human warmth that stood out sharply in a seinen magazine.

tondesaitama.title: Tonde Saitama
tondesaitama.desc: Let Saitama people eat the grass by the roadside! Affectionate hometown mockery that broke out all over again when it was filmed 30 years later.

cookingpapa.title: Cooking Papa
cookingpapa.desc: Kazumi Araiwa, a Hakata trading-company father who happens to be a fine cook. A long-running food manga, loved for recipes you can actually use.

chibimaruko.title: Chibi Maruko-chan
chibimaruko.desc: The author's own girlhood in Shimizu, Shizuoka, in 1974. It brought the sensibility of the essay into a girls' magazine, and became a national institution.

conan.title: Detective Conan
conan.desc: Shinichi Kudo, a high-school detective whose body has shrunk. A long-running mystery that widened the audience for the battle-of-wits manga to everyone.

rurouni.title: Rurouni Kenshin
rurouni.desc: Tokyo, 1878. Kenshin Himura, a former assassin sworn never to kill again. The high point of historical setting crossed with a Jump battle manga.

barakamon.title: Barakamon
barakamon.desc: A young calligrapher moves to the Goto Islands after failing in the city, and life among the islanders. A regional hit that began as a web serial.

ginsaji.title: Silver Spoon
ginsaji.desc: Hachiken flees an academic high school for an agricultural one in Hokkaido. A coming-of-age story that faces food and life head-on, and opened up a new kind of school manga.

sazae.title: Sazae-san
sazae.desc: The cornerstone of the newspaper four-panel strip, centred on the Isono family. It became the very image of the postwar Japanese household, and then a national anime.

tetsujin28.title: Tetsujin 28-go
tetsujin28.desc: A giant robot worked by remote control, and the boy Shotaro Kaneda. With Astro Boy, the origin of the giant-robot manga.

babil.title: Babel II
babil.desc: Koichi, who inherits the power of a superhuman from ancient Babylon, fights Yomi's bid for world conquest with three servants at his side. It drew telekinesis and telepathy as techniques, and became the template for psychic battle manga.

osomatsu.title: Osomatsu-kun
osomatsu.desc: A classic of gag manga, with sextuplets, Iyami and Chibita running riot. Its catchphrase entered the language, and it established the character-driven gag.

hinotori.title: Phoenix
hinotori.desc: Tezuka's life's work, drawing life and rebirth on a vast scale. Past and future chapters alternate, and the thought of the god of manga is concentrated in it.

doraemon.title: Doraemon
doraemon.desc: A cat-shaped robot from the future, and the gadgets he lends Nobita. The summit of children's manga, loved worldwide as a national character.

ginga999.title: Galaxy Express 999
ginga999.desc: Tetsuro and Maetel travel the galaxy in search of a mechanical body. Lyrical science fiction, an episode at a time, and the emblem of the 1970s anime boom.

kochikame.title: KochiKame: Tokyo Beat Cops
kochikame.desc: The chaos around Kankichi Ryotsu, an outrageous downtown policeman. Forty years and 200 volumes run to completion — a record-holding long-lived gag manga.

drslump.title: Dr. Slump
drslump.desc: Bottomlessly cheerful gags with an inventor and the robot girl Arale. Toriyama's drawing and taste laid the ground for Jump in the 1980s.

kinnikuman.title: Kinnikuman
kinnikuman.desc: Gags and pro-wrestling battles following the growth of a hopeless superhuman. Its cast of odd superhumans and their eraser figures became a social phenomenon.

captsubasa.title: Captain Tsubasa
captsubasa.desc: The ball is my friend. Tsubasa Ozora's football story, which influenced top professionals abroad and drove football's popularity in Japan.

seiya.title: Saint Seiya
seiya.desc: Boys in sacred cloth fight for the goddess Athena. A stylised beauty drawn from Greek myth and the constellations — and a merchandising hit.

jojo1.title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure Part 1: Phantom Blood
jojo1.desc: England, the 19th century. The beginning of the grudge between Jonathan Joestar and Dio, who means to take everything from him. A prologue of stone masks, Ripple, and the Joestar destiny.

jojo2.title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure Part 2: Battle Tendency
jojo2.desc: The eve of the Second World War. The freewheeling second-generation Joseph takes on the superhuman Pillar Men with Ripple. Tension and comedy side by side, in the part that settled the series' popularity.

jojo3.title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure Part 3: Stardust Crusaders
jojo3.desc: From Japan to Egypt, to strike down the revived DIO. It invented the Stand, and with it changed how boys' manga fights.

jojo4.title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure Part 4: Diamond is Unbreakable
jojo4.desc: A serial killer, Yoshikage Kira, hidden in the ordinary life of the fictional town of Morioh. Stand battles brought down into a neighbourhood mystery — the part many fans love best.

jojo5.title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure Part 5: Golden Wind
jojo5.desc: Italy. Giorno and his companions climb toward the top of a gang. A story of fate that resolves in Gold Experience Requiem, a Stand that controls time.

jojo6.title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure Part 6: Stone Ocean
jojo6.desc: A prison in Florida. Jolyne, wrongly imprisoned, reaches the end of DIO's grudge. The part that closes the destiny running through Parts 1 to 6.

jojo7.title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure Part 7: Steel Ball Run
jojo7.desc: America, 1890, and a race across the continent. A competition for the parts of a corpse, and a reset of the whole world of the series. Many call it the best, with Araki's drawing and structure at full maturity.

jojo8.title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure Part 8: JoJolion
jojo8.desc: Morioh after the earthquake. A mystery about the identity of Josuke, a man with no memory — another Morioh, and a curse that has to be undone.

jojo9.title: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure Part 9: The JOJOLands
jojo9.desc: Hawaii, present day. The bizarre adventure of Jodio, a boy who wants to be rich. The current part, still running.

cityhunter.title: City Hunter
cityhunter.desc: The hard-boiled comedy of Ryo Saeba, Shinjuku's crack sweeper. Adult glamour and gags in alternation brought seinen readers in too.

yuyu.title: Yu Yu Hakusho
yuyu.desc: The delinquent Yusuke Urameshi becomes a spirit detective. Spirit-energy battles and a memorable cast carried Jump through the early 1990s.

yugioh.title: Yu-Gi-Oh!
yugioh.desc: Games of darkness and card duels. The card game inside the story became a real worldwide product — a monument of the media mix.

hikaru.title: Hikaru no Go
hikaru.desc: The boy Hikaru and Sai, a ghost from the Heian court, take on the world of Go. It turned an unglamorous subject into fights you could not look away from, and set off a Go boom among children.

naruto.title: Naruto
naruto.desc: The hopeless ninja Naruto grows through his bonds with others. Ninjutsu battles and the theme of wanting to be recognised made it a worldwide hit.

prince_tennis.title: The Prince of Tennis
prince_tennis.desc: The prodigy Ryoma Echizen and middle-school tennis. Escalating special moves and beloved characters opened sports manga to a new readership.

eyeshield.title: Eyeshield 21
eyeshield.desc: The quick-footped Sena Kobayakawa takes on American football. An unusual sports manga that carried a minor sport on sheer drawing and strategy.

gintama.title: Gintama
gintama.desc: The odd-jobs man Gintoki Sakata, in an Edo the aliens have arrived in. The gap between all-out crude comedy and genuine seriousness earned it a fervent following.

masaru.title: Sexy Commando Gaiden: Sugoiyo!! Masaru-san
masaru.desc: Masaru and his cheerful club devote themselves to a mysterious martial art, Sexy Commando. Its surreal timing, cutting every thread of logic, was a gag revolution in 1990s Jump.

jaguar.title: Pyu to Fuku! Jaguar
jaguar.desc: A slack-limbed gag manga about being dragged around by Jaguar, a man who has given his life to the recorder. Ten years of run on the slow-burning wrongness of its dialogue — Usuta's gag form perfected.

kurobas.title: Kuroko's Basketball
kurobas.desc: Kuroko, the shadowy sixth man, and the Generation of Miracles playing basketball. Presentation borrowed from ability battles brought fresh air to sports manga.

haikyu.title: Haikyu!!
haikyu.desc: The small Shoyo Hinata takes on high-school volleyball. Precise match drawing and a large ensemble made it the representative sports manga of the 2010s.

hero_aca.title: My Hero Academia
hero_aca.desc: In a world where everyone has a Quirk, the quirkless Izuku Midoriya sets out to be the greatest hero. An American-comics sensibility won it a worldwide audience.

promised.title: The Promised Neverland
promised.desc: Children use their wits against the truth hidden inside an orphanage that calls itself a farm. A much-discussed work fusing battles of wits with a dark world.

jujutsu.title: Jujutsu Kaisen
jujutsu.desc: Sorcerers fighting curses to the death. Cursed spirits born of negative feeling, plus a contemporary sense of staging, made it the defining Jump hit of the Reiwa years.

nigeue.title: The Elusive Samurai
nigeue.desc: Hojo Tokiyuki, a boy who loses everything when the Kamakura shogunate falls, aims for the top armed only with his one talent: running away. Yusei Matsui turned the Nanboku-cho period, long thought unglamorous, into a battlefield for boys' manga.

ellen.title: Left-handed Ellen
ellen.desc: Koichi Asakura, a designer at an ad agency, and Ellen Yamagishi, a genius painter. Written for everyone who did not turn out to be a genius, it follows people making peace with envy and carrying on working — a web-born ensemble piece about creators.

fma.title: Fullmetal Alchemist
fma.desc: Two brothers who lost their bodies to alchemy, on the road. The theme of equivalent exchange and tightly repaid foreshadowing make it one of the most complete works a monthly boys' magazine has produced.

dai.title: Dragon Quest: The Adventure of Dai
dai.desc: The adventure of the hero Dai, set in the world of the Dragon Quest games. Still loved as the finished form of the mainline fantasy battle manga.

ranma.title: Ranma 1/2
ranma.desc: A martial-arts romantic comedy around Ranma, a boy who becomes a girl when splashed with water. Takahashi's signature work, with an enormous following at home and abroad.

inuyasha.title: Inuyasha
inuyasha.desc: Kagome, a modern girl who slips into the Warring States period, and the half-demon Inuyasha. A long work fusing yokai with romance, and a landmark of the 1990s and 2000s.

maison.title: Maison Ikkoku
maison.desc: The maddeningly slow romance between Kyoko, who manages an old apartment building, and Godai, a student retaking his exams. The cornerstone of seinen romantic comedy.

ushiotora.title: Ushio and Tora
ushiotora.desc: The mismatched pair of the boy Ushio and the yokai Tora take on great demons. Fierce friendship and forceful drawing make it a masterpiece of the yokai battle manga.

major.title: Major
major.desc: Goro Honda's life in baseball, from childhood to the majors. The representative long-form sports story following one player's whole career.

kindaichi.title: The Kindaichi Case Files
kindaichi.desc: Hajime, grandson of a great detective, takes on hard cases. It brought locked rooms and logic puzzles to a boys' magazine and set off a boom.

ippo.title: Hajime no Ippo
ippo.desc: Ippo Makunouchi, once bullied, grows up through boxing. Careful drawing of matches and of training has kept it loved for decades.

tokyorev.title: Tokyo Revengers
tokyorev.desc: Time-leaping into the past to save his girlfriend and his best friend, through gang warfare. Delinquents plus time travel made it a phenomenon.

bluelock.title: Blue Lock
bluelock.desc: A ruthless project to raise the world's most selfish striker. Values that overturn the usual team-first sports story won over a new generation.

frieren.title: Frieren: Beyond Journey's End
frieren.desc: Frieren, a long-lived elf mage, living in the world after the demon king has fallen. A quiet story of death, time and understanding other people — the story of what comes after the adventure.

berserk.title: Berserk
berserk.desc: The dark medieval fantasy of the swordsman Guts, his revenge and his causality. Ferocious detail and a weighty story make it the summit of dark fantasy.

ghost.title: Ghost in the Shell
ghost.desc: Motoko Kusanagi and her public-security unit in a cyberised society. A worldwide cyberpunk classic questioning the borders of information, body and consciousness.

twentieth.title: 20th Century Boys
twentieth.desc: A book of prophecy made up in childhood turns out to connect to a real conspiracy. Nostalgia for boyhood and an enormous mystery kept readers gripped.

yawara.title: Yawara!
yawara.desc: The daily life and competitions of Yawara Inokuma, a judo prodigy. A light-footed seinen sports romance that caught the air of the bubble years.

vagabond.title: Vagabond
vagabond.desc: Based on Eiji Yoshikawa's Musashi, on a swordsman's life and what strength is for. Overwhelming brushwork lifted period gekiga to a new height.

hyouge.title: Hyouge Mono
hyouge.desc: The life of Furuta Oribe, a warlord who tried to survive the Warring States not by arms but by suki — tea and beauty. Comic in his helplessness before great lords and famous tea vessels, and abnormal in his attachment to beauty, it brought aesthetics into historical manga as a subject.

kingdom.title: Kingdom
kingdom.desc: Ancient China at the end of the Warring States period, where the servant boy Xin sets out to become a great general. A vast war chronicle and ensemble drama, and one of the biggest hits a seinen magazine has had.

vinland.title: Vinland Saga
vinland.desc: 11th-century Scandinavia, where the young Thorfinn, living for revenge, slowly turns into a true warrior. A Viking epic grounded in history.

planetes.title: Planetes
planetes.desc: Near-future science fiction about the people who collect debris in orbit. A lyrical masterpiece that draws both the reality of space development and the inner life quietly.

uchukyodai.title: Space Brothers
uchukyodai.desc: Two brothers who want to be astronauts. Dreams and setbacks drawn with adult realism, and admired by people actually working in space.

goldenkamuy.title: Golden Kamuy
goldenkamuy.desc: Hokkaido in the late Meiji years, where an ex-soldier and an Ainu girl chase a hoard of gold. An adventure like no other, packed with Ainu culture, hunting, food and comedy.

tokyoghoul.title: Tokyo Ghoul
tokyoghoul.desc: The torment of Kaneki, a young man who becomes a ghoul, a species that eats people. The space between human and monster, drawn with an aesthete's line.

kaguya.title: Kaguya-sama: Love Is War
kaguya.desc: The student council president and vice-president, both brilliant, wage a war of wits in which confessing first means losing. The defining romantic comedy of the Reiwa years.

sangatsu.title: March Comes in Like a Lion
sangatsu.desc: Rei Kiriyama, a lonely young shogi professional, recovering through the game and through other people. Delicate psychological drawing lifts shogi into human drama.

ooku.title: Ooku: The Inner Chambers
ooku.desc: An alternate history in which the roles of the sexes are reversed and the shogun is a woman. Widely praised for its careful period research and its thinking about gender.

kinou.title: What Did You Eat Yesterday?
kinou.desc: The daily life and the dinner table of a middle-aged gay couple, drawn plainly. Loved by a wide readership for its usable recipes and its life-sized living.

uzumaki.title: Uzumaki
uzumaki.desc: Junji Ito's signature work, on the strangeness that grips a town possessed by the spiral. A worldwide cult following for its unreasonable, beautiful images of fear.

dorohedoro.title: Dorohedoro
dorohedoro.desc: A chaotic world where sorcerers and the residents of the Hole cross paths. Detailed, deformed world-building and black comedy have earned it devoted fans.

mob.title: Mob Psycho 100
mob.desc: The growth of Mob, an unremarkable boy with enormous psychic power. A popular web-born work by ONE, the author of One Punch Man.

ace_nerae.title: Aim for the Ace!
ace_nerae.desc: The ordinary girl Hiromi Oka throws herself into tennis under a hard coach. It fused sports-and-guts with shojo manga and shaped much of what followed.

candy.title: Candy Candy
candy.desc: A sweeping romance following the eventful life of Candy, an orphan girl. One of the defining shojo manga of the 1970s, and enormously popular.

hanadan.title: Boys Over Flowers
hanadan.desc: A love story between the working-class Tsukushi and F4, a group of rich heirs. One of the best-selling shojo manga of all time.

nana.title: Nana
nana.desc: Love, dreams and friendship between two women who share the name Nana. A landmark of josei manga, with a charismatic following built on music and life-sized youth.

fruits.title: Fruits Basket
fruits.desc: The Soma family, under the curse of the zodiac, and the girl Tohru. A careful account of hurt hearts recovering, and one of shojo manga's biggest sellers.

ccs.title: Cardcaptor Sakura
ccs.desc: The story of Sakura Kinomoto, a magical girl collecting cards. Sweetness and a wardrobe of costumes made it a new classic of the magical-girl form.

kimitodoke.title: Kimi ni Todoke: From Me to You
kimitodoke.desc: The first love and friendships of Sawako, a girl everyone misreads. Its purity of feeling made it a defining shojo manga of the 2000s.

chihaya.title: Chihayafuru
chihaya.desc: Chihaya and her friends staking their youth on competitive karuta. Shojo manga fused with sports-and-guts, and the cause of a karuta boom.

nodame.title: Nodame Cantabile
nodame.desc: A classical-music romantic comedy between the unruly pianist Nodame and Chiaki, who wants to conduct. Set in a music college, it drove a boom in classical music.

hachikuro.title: Honey and Clover
hachikuro.desc: The unrequited loves and youth of art-college students, drawn freshly. Its balance of ache and humour is where the author's later work begins.

crayon.title: Crayon Shin-chan
crayon.desc: The crude, precocious gags of the five-year-old Shinnosuke. A national anime and the standard-bearer of everyday gag manga, loved across generations.

bobobo.title: Bobobo-bo Bo-bobo
bobobo.desc: The absurdist gags of Bobobo, who fights with nose-hair techniques. High tension beyond all reason, and a cult following.

hiwa.title: Gag Manga Biyori
hiwa.desc: Slack-limbed short gags built on historical figures and the like. Its particular rhythm and surrealism earned it an anime too.

yotsuba.title: Yotsuba&!
yotsuba.desc: Yotsuba, a girl made entirely of curiosity, and the unremarkable days of the people around her. The high point of slice-of-life, by the author of Azumanga Daioh.

keion.title: K-On!
keion.desc: Four-panel strips about the easy days of the girls in a light-music club. The anime made it a phenomenon and created the slice-of-life-plus-band boom.

yurucamp.title: Yuru Camp
yurucamp.desc: Girls camping gently outdoors in winter. Careful landscape drawing and a restful air made it the spark for a camping boom.

bakabon.title: Genius Bakabon
bakabon.desc: This is fine, as it is. The destructive nonsense of Bakabon's papa, and the representative work of Akatsuka's comedy, familiar across generations.

gakideka.title: Gaki Deka
gakideka.desc: The crude, extreme gags of Komawari-kun, a boy policeman. His death-sentence pose came to stand for the gag revolution of the 1970s.

macaroni.title: Makaroni Horenso
macaroni.desc: Frenzied comedy packed with high tension and parody. A legendary work that shaped the speed of the gag manga that followed.

kimenzu.title: High School! Kimengumi
kimenzu.desc: School gags with the five distinct members of the Kimengumi. A favourite that carried Jump's comedy line through the 1980s.

cobra.title: Cobra
cobra.desc: The exploits of the space pirate Cobra and his Psychogun. An early Japanese space opera in the American-comics mould, and very popular.

dokaben.title: Dokaben
dokaben.desc: A high-school baseball ensemble centred on Taro Yamada. Precise match drawing built an era of the baseball manga across a long run.

captain_chiba.title: Captain
captain_chiba.desc: Middle-school baseball, in which ordinary players become strong through work. An honest sports story with no flash, still highly regarded.

ring.title: Ring ni Kakero
ring.desc: Boxing with finishing blows that detonate. It brought superhuman staging into sports-and-guts, and became the template for the author's later work and for shonen battles.

rookies.title: Rookies
rookies.desc: A hot-blooded teacher rebuilds a baseball team full of delinquents. Sweat, tears and youth won it a wide following.

hoshin.title: Hoshin Engi
hoshin.desc: Immortal battles adapted boldly from the Chinese classics. Stylish drawing and a reading of its own earned it a cult following.

reborn.title: Reborn!
reborn.desc: Tsuna, a hopeless middle-schooler, is dragged into training as a mafia boss. Its turn from comedy into full battle manga made it popular.

toriko.title: Toriko
toriko.desc: The gourmet hunter Toriko hunts for ultimate ingredients. A boisterous world fusing food with battle.

ansatsu.title: Assassination Classroom
ansatsu.desc: A school story about assassinating Koro-sensei, a mysterious creature who has announced he will destroy the earth. An unusual work built on teaching and growth.

souma.title: Food Wars!: Shokugeki no Soma
souma.desc: Soma Yukihira takes on shokugeki, cooking duels. Battle manga's heat poured into cooking, in a popular Jump food series.

dgray.title: D.Gray-man
dgray.desc: Exorcists fighting the demons called AKUMA. Gothic, detailed world-building and a beloved cast won it its readers.

kaiju8.title: Kaiju No. 8
kaiju8.desc: A middle-aged man who gains the power of a kaiju fights in the defence force. A new-generation hit, popular at home and abroad at once, from a web serial.

oshinoko.title: Oshi no Ko
oshinoko.desc: A man reborn as an idol's child takes on the dark side of show business. Reincarnation plus entertainment plus suspense made it a phenomenon.

sakamoto.title: Sakamoto Days
sakamoto.desc: Sakamoto, a legendary retired hitman, fights to protect his family. Popular for its refined action staging.

dandadan.title: Dandadan
dandadan.desc: A youth battle manga where the occult and aliens collide. Overwhelming drawing and pace made it a much-discussed web-born hit.

h2.title: H2
h2.desc: Baseball and a four-way tangle between childhood friends. Adachi's summing-up of the youth-baseball romance.

kyoukara.title: From Today, It's My Turn!!
kyoukara.desc: Delinquent gags about two boys who debut as thugs after transferring schools. Well-timed comedy and fights have kept it loved.

diamond.title: Ace of Diamond
diamond.desc: Eijun Sawamura, a pitcher growing up in a famous baseball club. A serious baseball manga that takes the tension of fighting for a position seriously.

nanatsu.title: The Seven Deadly Sins
nanatsu.desc: The adventures of the legendary knights called the Seven Deadly Sins. A mainline fantasy battle manga, and a worldwide hit.

gotoubun.title: The Quintessential Quintuplets
gotoubun.desc: A boy tutoring quintuplets, and where his love ends up. Readers were gripped by the question of which one he chooses.

ajin.title: Ajin: Demi-Human
ajin.desc: The struggle around the ajin, a new kind of human that cannot die. Cold-blooded battles of wits and action made it a seinen hit.

initiald.title: Initial D
initiald.desc: A street-racing manga about attacking mountain passes. It produced a drifting boom and became the emblem of street-racing culture.

mushishi.title: Mushishi
mushishi.desc: A fantasy about the relationship between mushi and people. A cycle of short stories highly praised for its still, poetic world.

blueperiod.title: Blue Period
blueperiod.desc: Yatora, who does everything competently, is struck by a single painting and enters the world of art-school entrance exams. It faces the pain and the joy of betting your life on what you love, and turned art into a youth sport.

eizouken.title: Keep Your Hands Off Eizouken!
eizouken.desc: Asakusa the setting obsessive, Mizusaki the charismatic reader-model, and Kanamori who handles the money, take on making anime to build the strongest world. The imagined images erupt straight onto the page, and the pleasure of making things comes through whole.

thermae.title: Thermae Romae
thermae.desc: Lucius, a bath engineer of ancient Rome, keeps slipping forward into modern Japanese baths. Flattened by the flat-faced tribe's technology, he takes each idea home — a comparative-culture comedy that does history and civilisation entirely through bathing.

historie.title: Historie
historie.desc: The life of Eumenes, a scribe of ancient Greece. A meticulous historical epic by Hitoshi Iwaaki, the author of Parasyte.

baki.title: Grappler Baki
baki.desc: The death matches of Baki Hanma, a fighter in search of being strongest. Excessive anatomy and a fighting theory of its own have earned it a cult following.

akagi.title: Akagi
akagi.desc: The mahjong and the manner of living of the prodigy Shigeru Akagi. A philosophy of games played with your life on the table, at the summit of mahjong gekiga.

ten.title: Ten
ten.desc: How men live, told through mahjong. The death of Shigeru Akagi in the later chapters, and the conversations around it, are among gekiga's finest scenes.

kintaro.title: Salaryman Kintaro
kintaro.desc: A former biker-gang leader turned salaryman moves a company by speaking plainly and acting. The standard-bearer of the satisfying business manga.

pluto.title: Pluto
pluto.desc: Naoki Urasawa's remake of The Greatest Robot on Earth from Tezuka's Astro Boy. A weighty masterpiece on robots and war.

kodoku.title: The Solitary Gourmet
kodoku.desc: A story in which a middle-aged man simply eats alone. No showy expertise, no incident — it opened new ground on the richness of just eating.

shinya.title: Midnight Diner
shinya.desc: An ensemble of human warmth around the people who gather at a small diner open only late at night. A neighbourhood drama told one dish at a time.

beck.title: Beck
beck.desc: Koyuki, an unremarkable middle-schooler, meets the prodigy guitarist Ryusuke and joins the band BECK. It made readers believe in sound they could not hear, and brought the heat of Western rock into a Japanese boys' magazine.

bluegiant.title: Blue Giant
bluegiant.desc: A boy who means to become the best jazz player in the world. Highly praised for performance scenes that let you hear sound through drawing.

kusuriya.title: The Apothecary Diaries
kusuriya.desc: Maomao, a girl who solves incidents in the rear palace with her knowledge of medicine. A huge hit as a Chinese-style mystery in adaptation.

animal_doctor.title: Animal Doctor
animal_doctor.desc: A slack-limbed comedy set in a Hokkaido veterinary faculty. An unusual entry for a girls' magazine, and the cause of a Siberian husky boom.

patalliro.title: Patalliro!
patalliro.desc: The gags Patalliro, the eternally young king, sets off, and his beautiful spies. Known as a long-running comedy in a girls' magazine and a forerunner of BL.

yona.title: Yona of the Dawn
yona.desc: The growth and adventures of Princess Yona, driven from her country. A fantasy epic that widened what shojo manga could hold.

basara.title: Basara
basara.desc: In a Japan after civilisation has fallen, Sarasa plays the child of destiny in place of her twin brother, and leads a revolution. An epic that brought sturdy war chronicle and nation-building into shojo manga.

7seeds.title: 7Seeds
7seeds.desc: Young people wake in a Japan after a meteor strike, and have to survive. Sixteen years and 35 volumes of apocalyptic science fiction inside the shojo form, and a Shogakukan Manga Award.

mystery_nakare.title: Don't Call It Mystery
mystery_nakare.desc: Totono Kuno, a university student who keeps getting caught up in things, unpicks incidents and people's assumptions not by deduction but by asking back. An unusual work that turns conversation itself into the detective story.

ouran.title: Ouran High School Host Club
ouran.desc: Haruhi, a girl caught up in the host club of an elite school. The standard-bearer of the reverse-harem comedy.

tarareba.title: Tokyo Tarareba Girls
tarareba.desc: The love lives and the panic of women around thirty, drawn severely and comically at once. Life-sized recognition won it an overwhelming female readership.

sekaiichi.title: The World's Greatest First Love
sekaiichi.desc: A popular working-adult BL set in an editorial department. A representative series of commercial BL's expansion.

lucky.title: Lucky Star
lucky.desc: Easygoing four-panel strips about otaku high-school girls. The anime produced a pilgrimage boom and came to stand for slice-of-life culture.

saint_oniisan.title: Saint Young Men
saint_oniisan.desc: An easygoing comedy in which Buddha and Jesus share a flat down here on earth. Its light touch with religion made it popular.

nichijou.title: Nichijou: My Ordinary Life
nichijou.desc: Gags in which a flat everyday suddenly collapses into surrealism. Its particular timing and absurdity have devoted fans.

relife.title: ReLIFE
relife.desc: A young man not in work or education takes a pill and returns to high school to do it again. An early hit from the vertical-scroll full-colour apps.

rezero.title: Re:Zero - Starting Life in Another World
rezero.desc: Subaru struggles in a hopeless other world armed with return by death, which rewinds time whenever he dies. One of the defining works to come out of the web-novel sites.

overlord.title: Overlord
overlord.desc: A man left behind in a game world as a skeletal overlord, and his conquest. The standard-bearer of the too-strong-protagonist other-world story.

tatenoyusha.title: The Rising of the Shield Hero
tatenoyusha.desc: A hero given nothing but a shield he cannot attack with, betrayed, and taking his revenge. The work that lit the exile-and-revenge branch of web novels.

mushoku.title: Mushoku Tensei: Jobless Reincarnation
mushoku.desc: A recluse restarts life in another world from infancy. A reincarnation chronicle often called the monument of the web-novel form.

konosuba.title: KonoSuba: God's Blessing on This Wonderful World!
konosuba.desc: Other-world comedy with a set of useless goddesses. The standard slack comedy parodying the web-novel genre itself.

madoka.title: Puella Magi Madoka Magica
madoka.desc: A shocking work that inverts the magical girl's wish and despair. Cruelty behind a sweet drawing style rewrote what a magical girl could be.

precure.title: Futari wa Pretty Cure
precure.desc: Two middle-schoolers who fight with their fists. The transforming heroines at the origin of the long-running Pretty Cure series.

naniwa.title: Naniwa Kinyudo
naniwa.desc: Human greed and the loopholes in the law, seen from the floor of a back-street lending firm. Financial gekiga that recorded the reality of the years the bubble burst.

investorz.title: Investor Z
investorz.desc: Middle-schoolers running their school's endowment in an investment club. An informational manga that teaches money and economics through story.

dragonzakura.title: Dragon Zakura
dragonzakura.desc: A strategy drama about getting into the University of Tokyo from a failing high school. The byword for the study-method manga.

ginto.title: Gin to Kin
ginto.desc: A psychological contest over large sums in the underworld. The origin point of Fukumoto's gambling gekiga, leading to Akagi and Kaiji.

tetsuya.title: Tetsuya: Legend of a Mahjong Genius
tetsuya.desc: Tetsuya, a mahjong drifter crossing the burnt-out postwar cities. A gambler's chronicle that records both the heat of the game and the smell of the Showa years.

kakegurui.title: Kakegurui: Compulsive Gambler
kakegurui.desc: A crazed transfer student arrives at a school where gambling decides everything. A Reiwa hit that goes all in on the pleasure of gambling and on facial acting.

utsurun.title: Utsurun Desu
utsurun.desc: Absurd laughter with no thread of logic. The book that drove the absurdist gag boom of the 1990s.

bonobono.title: Bonobono
bonobono.desc: Gentle, philosophical four-panel strips about the otter child Bonobono and his friends in the forest. A long-running work where comfort and absurdity live together.

lychee.title: Litchi Hikari Club
lychee.desc: Aestheticism and violence around Litchi, a machine built by a group of boys. A cult subculture manga adapted from underground theatre.

shojotsubaki.title: Shojo Tsubaki (Mr. Arashi's Amazing Freak Show)
shojotsubaki.desc: The suffering of Midori, a girl sold to a freak show. Ero-guro and Taisho romanticism crossing — a cornerstone of underground manga.

kaminotou.title: Tower of God
kaminotou.desc: A boy climbing a tower to have his wish granted. A worldwide hit Korean webtoon, and the work that spread vertical scrolling globally.

megami.title: True Beauty
megami.desc: The love life and self-acceptance of a girl who becomes a goddess through makeup. A representative hit of the vertical-scroll shojo manga.

otakoi.title: Wotakoi: Love Is Hard for Otaku
otakoi.desc: The awkward adult romance of two otaku. A Reiwa romantic comedy that started on pixiv, went round on social media and was then published.

baptism.title: Baptism
baptism.desc: A mother obsessed with her own beauty tries to take her daughter's body. The representative Umezu horror, which brought trauma-grade fear into girls' manga.

kobochan.title: Kobo-chan
kobochan.desc: A newspaper four-panel standard about the kindergartener Kobo and his family. A national work read across generations.

jungle.title: Jungle Emperor Leo
jungle.desc: The story of three generations of Leo, a white lion. An early high point of the long-form story manga, and the origin of colour anime in Japan.

akko.title: Himitsu no Akko-chan
akko.desc: Akko, a girl who can become anything through her mirror. One of the ancestors of the magical-girl form, and Akatsuka's hit in a girls' magazine.

akairo.title: Red Colored Elegy
akairo.desc: A young couple living poorly together, and parting. Lyrical line work that stands for Garo's poetic realism.

toma.title: The Heart of Thomas
toma.desc: A story of the soul, around a boy's death at a German boarding school. The cornerstone of the Year 24 Group's writing on boys' love and interiority.

domu.title: Domu: A Child's Dream
domu.desc: An old man and a girl fight with psychic power in a housing estate. Meticulous drawing and quiet destruction renewed Japanese science-fiction manga.

sangokushi.title: Sangokushi (Records of the Three Kingdoms)
sangokushi.desc: From the upheavals at the end of the Later Han through the three kingdoms to Jin's unification. Sixty volumes based on Eiji Yoshikawa's version, and the work that settled how Japanese readers picture the Three Kingdoms.

akira.desc: Psychic power and a collapsed Tokyo drawn with overwhelming skill. The cyberpunk monument that turned MANGA into a word the world uses.

slam.desc: The delinquent Hanamichi Sakuragi discovers basketball. It updated the genes of sports-and-guts with realism and set off a basketball boom in Japan.

onepiece.desc: Luffy's voyage to become King of the Pirates. Holder of the world record for the most copies of a comic by a single author, and Jump's mainline in its present form.

deathnote.desc: Light Yagami, a genius who picks up a notebook that kills whoever's name is written in it, against L. It opened new ground for boys' manga with tension and no fighting at all.

hxh.desc: Gon sets out to become a Hunter and find his absent father Ging. With the meticulous rule design of Nen and fights decided by cunning rather than force, it keeps raising the bar for battle manga.

bleach.desc: Ichigo Kurosaki fights after gaining the power of a Soul Reaper. Refined page composition and character design made it a flagship of 2000s Jump.

drstone.desc: Senku rebuilds a world where humanity has turned to stone, using science. A new angle — winning through science — brought intellectual excitement to a boys' magazine.

spyfamily.desc: A spy, a telepath and an assassin play at being a family. A web serial that became an enormous hit across every age group.

gto.desc: Eikichi Onizuka, an ex-biker turned unorthodox teacher, rebuilds a classroom that has fallen apart. A satisfying school drama with a following across generations.

fairytail.desc: The adventures of the wizards' guild Fairy Tail. Bonds between companions and mainline magic battles won it a worldwide readership.

monster.desc: A boy the genius surgeon Tenma saved becomes a serial killer. A weighty human drama and suspense set across Germany.

uw-1783194623967-059g.title: Parasyte

12C—1860s.title: Prehistory — the tradition of telling with pictures
12C—1860s.body: The late-Heian Choju-jinbutsu-giga has rabbits and frogs wrestling in ink line alone, making comedy and story out of pictures with nothing else. In the Edo period Toba-e and kusazoshi became popular entertainment, and in 1814 Hokusai published his sketchbook Hokusai Manga and spread the word manga. None of these have panels or speech balloons, so the bloodline to modern manga is thin — but the soil of a culture that reads pictures was grown here.

1900s—1930s.title: Modern manga is born
1900s—1930s.body: It starts with Rakuten Kitazawa's satirical drawings, and the grammar of panels and balloons settles in the newspaper serial Shochan no Boken. Norakuro in Shonen Club became the biggest hit of the prewar years, and a culture in which children read manga came into being. On street corners kamishibai flourished, training the gekiga artists to come.

1945—1955.title: Tezuka and the story-manga revolution
1945—1955.body: Amid the flood of cheap akahon manga in postwar Osaka, New Treasure Island in 1947 electrified young readers with cinematic panel work. Osamu Tezuka established story manga — telling a long narrative in comics — and with Astro Boy and Princess Knight made the templates for both boys' and girls' manga. The next generation of talent gathered at Tokiwa-so.

1955—1965.title: Rental books, and the arrival of gekiga
1955—1965.body: Volumes drawn specifically for rental shops formed a market of their own. Out of it, Yoshihiro Tatsumi and the Gekiga Kobo group declared gekiga: realistic manga for adults, set against Tezuka's round line. In 1959 Weekly Shonen Magazine and Sunday launched on the same day and the age of weekly serialisation began. In 1964 Garo was founded for Sanpei Shirato, and became the sanctuary of the alternative.

1966—1975.title: The heat of sports-and-guts, and the Year 24 revolution
1966—1975.body: Star of the Giants and Tomorrow's Joe brought gekiga's heat into boys' magazines, and dramas of effort and sheer will swept the decade. In shojo manga, Moto Hagio, Keiko Takemiya and the rest of the Year 24 Group brought interior monologue, science fiction and boys' love, and lifted the form to a literary height. The Rose of Versailles became a social phenomenon. Seinen magazines launched one after another, and the reader's age widened all at once.

1976—1985.title: Romantic comedy, New Wave, diversification
1976—1985.body: Rumiko Takahashi and Mitsuru Adachi carried shojo manga's grammar of romance into boys' magazines and romantic comedy bloomed. Otomo's AKIRA startled the world with a line that belonged neither to gekiga nor to Tezuka. In seinen magazines, Oishinbo and Section Chief Kosaku Shima invented the adult-practical genres of food and business. Manga became reading for every age.

1985—1995.title: Jump's golden age
1985—1995.body: With Dragon Ball, Fist of the North Star and SLAM DUNK, Weekly Shonen Jump reached a peak circulation of 6.53 million copies in 1995. The formula of friendship, effort and victory plus the tournament arc was complete. In girls' magazines, Sailor Moon created the fighting-beautiful-girl heroine and rewrote girls' culture worldwide.

1995—2005.title: Fragmentation, and the subculture years
1995—2005.body: Jump's dominance broke and genres split rapidly. Kaiji's psychological extremes, the slice-of-life Azumanga Daioh invented, DEATH NOTE's battles of wits, the comic essay of My Darling is a Foreigner — each niche began evolving on its own. Manga cafes and second-hand chains changed how manga was read, too.

2005—2015.title: The web, a new continent
2005—2015.body: One Punch Man, born on a personal website, became a hit by leaping over existing distribution. Attack on Titan went from a minor magazine to a social phenomenon, and huge hits from outside Jump became normal. E-books and phone apps spread, and adaptations of web novels — the isekai boom — grew into a major industry.

2015—現在.title: Global, and the age of social media
2015—現在.body: Demon Slayer produced a historic boom together with its anime, and a new generation led by Chainsaw Man keeps updating what Jump can be. Korean vertical-scroll webtoons grew fast through Piccoma and LINE Manga, and A Crocodile That Lives 100 Days, born on Twitter, made social media itself part of the story. Japanese manga is now at a point where the publishing format itself is the frontier.
